Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Judgement
01.

This case has in its background the complexities argued and amplified very temptingly by the learned counsel from both sides with best of their legal acumen but this court self commends itself with a caveat to stay away from dealing with those complexities lest that may cause a potential prejudice to the respective position of both contesting sides at any later point of time in their litigation battle which is still to have its final end.
Instead, this court is reserving itself to deal with the matter to the extent the case in hand admits of indulgence from the Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents 1 to 4, as being the plaintiffs, filed a civil suit on File no. 48/Civil on 25.01.2011[ before the Court of Sub Judge, Ramban.

In this civil suit, there were nine defendants starting from the State of J&K joined by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban as being the Collector Land Acquisition, 4 Lanes National Highway with rest of the defendants as being private ones.
The defendant no. 3 was Gh. Mohi-ud-Din Mir, who is the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner herein.

03. During the pendency of the civil suit, said Gh. Mohi-ud-Din Mir came to demise resulting in impleadment of his legal representatives who are his sons and the petitioner being one of them getting so impleaded.

04. In the civil suit, the respondents 1 to 4 sought a decree of declaration to the effect that they and the defendants 3 to 9 are the owners and co-sharers of the land under khasra no. 892/806 measuring 7.16 kanals, khasra no. 892/817 measuring 9.10 kanals and khasra no. 896/818 measuring 23.2 kanals in village Tulbagh Nagam, tehsil Banihal, district Ramban and for permanent prohibitory injunction to restrain the defendants 1 to 2 from disbursing the amount of compensation of the suit land being joint land of the respondents 1 to 4 and the defendants 3 to 9 which has come under four lanes National Highway.
05.
In the said suit, the court of Sub Judge, Ramban came to decree the suit by its judgement dated 30.11.2019.

Decree dated 30.11.2019 as drawn is stating that the plaintiffs, who are the respondents 1 to 4 herein, are declared as co-owners and co-sharers of the suit land and they are also entitled for compensation of the acquired land from the office of the defendant no. 2, who being the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban as being the then Collector Land Acquisition, to the extent of the respondents 1 to 4's shares and further injuncting the defendant no. 2 not to release the entire compensation in favour of the defendants 3 to 9 only by ignoring the right of the respondents 1 to 4.
06.

During the pendency of suit, the trial court of Sub Judge, Ramban, vide its order dated 28.02.2012, had restrained the official defendants 1 & 2 from disbursing compensation amount to the defendants 3 to 9.
07.
The decree is now said to be entangled in a proceeding before the Court of Sub Judge Ramban which has been initiated by the petitioner who is seeking its setting aside.
In this proceeding before the court of Sub Judge, Ramban there is no stay granted with respect to the operation of the decree.

08. Similarly, there are two civil first appeals preferred by non- parties to the suit against the said decree in which also there is no stay in place from the appellate court of Principal District Judge,
Ramban against the operation of the said decree.

09. The cause of action for the respondents 1 to 4 institute the civil suit was a corresponding development in which the suit land in reference was intended to be acquired under the J&K Land Acquisition Act, 1990 Svt., with issuance of section 4 notification dated 27.04.2010 which had given the respondents 1 to 4 an apprehension that they may not figure in the column of compensation claimants for the proposed acquisition of the suit land for the purpose of four laning of the national Bashir Ahmed Mir vs Gh. Hassan Mir And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172923037/
2 highway.
10.

In the backdrop of this situation post passing of the decree dated 30.11.2019 in the suit, afresh land acquisition proceedings came to take place resulting in passing of an Order no. CLA/NH- 44/2022/1079-82 dated 15.10.2022 with revised land market valuation passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban as being the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition purportedly acting under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text:
As per the Order no. CLA/NH-44/2022/1079-82 dated 15.10.2022, total compensation payable for 18.3 kanals of land in khasra nos. 892/806, 892/817 & 896/818 is 6,68,51,195/- out of which the compensation paid in first round of land acquisition was 34,27,100/- thereby leaving compensation amount of 4,43,96,838/- to be disbursed to the claimants.
12.
In this order dated 15/10/2022, the names of the respondents 1 to 4 per se did not find mention quo the acquired suit land in the award statement.

The amount of enhanced compensation came to be made available by the National Highway Authority (NHA) at the disposal of the Collectorate and which was pending disbursement to the entitled land owners.

13. The respondents 1 to 4 came forward with filing of an application purportedly for initiation of contempt proceedings against the contemnor named as Mr. Harbans Lal, as being the Additional Deputy Commissioner with power of Collector Land Acquisition, for wilful disobedience of judgement and decree dated 30.11.2019 as passed in civil suit titled Gh. Hassan & others Vs State of J&K and others.

entities.text: Gh. Hassan & others Vs State of J&K and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
14. This application came to be filed on 20.03.2023 on file no. 31/Civil/Misc., before the Court of Sub Judge, Ramban which, vide its order dated 20.03.2023, came to put the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban on notice for appearance on 28.03.2023 and then for 24.05.2023.
15.

It is at this stage of the proceedings in said application before the Sub Judge, Ramban that the petitioner rushed to approach this Court with the present petition filed on 15.05.2023 possibly apprehending that the court of Sub Judge, Ramban may come to seek compliance of the decree dated 30.11.2019 by directing Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to release the share-wise compensation of the respondents 1 to 4 as per the decree mandate.

16. In this petition, the petitioner assailed the legality of the proceedings so taken on its file by the court of Sub Judge, Ramban and passing of first two interim orders of summoning dated 20.03.2023 and next date 28.03.2023.

The petitioner has sought the quashment of proceedings along with two orders dated 20/03/2023 & 28/03/2023 by asking this court to exercise supervisory Bashir Ahmed Mir vs Gh. Hassan Mir And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172923037/
3 jurisdiction under article 227 of the Constitution of India.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. This Court came to take cognizance of this petition when vide an order dated 19.05.2023 came to direct the freezing of the bank accounts of the respondents 1 to 4 to which the disbursement of compensation amount as per their purported share was pleaded to have taken place out of the deposited compensation amount pre- empting the petitioner approaching this court for any injunctory direction.

18. This court directed the personal appearance of Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban with the record so as to know as to how the payment of the amount had come to take place.
In the meanwhile, the respondents 1 to 4 also came to cause their appearance through the counsel by submitting their reply.
Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban also submitted his reply supported with an affidavit.
19. Upon arguments from both sides, many shades of situations with legal ramifications cropped up.
All those submissions were duly registered by this court.

However, bearing in mind the realization that this court, at the best, was seized only of a petition under article 227 of the Constitution of India that too only with respect to taking of cognizance of application of the respondents 1 to 4 by the court of Sub Judge, Ramban and order of issuance of notice therein, this court self realized the limitation of dealing with the said shades of situations when the scope of the petition cannot reach those shades except by crossing Lakshman Rekha of jurisdiction.

20. This Court, nevertheless, examined the record as to circumstances which led the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to release the compensation amount to the respondents 1 to 4.
21.

The record reveals that the respondents 1 to 4 had submitted an application dated 28.02.2023 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban (with powers of Collector Land Acquisition,
Ramban) asking for release of compensation amount in compliance to the judgement and decree dated 30.11.2019.

This application came to be supplemented by submission of Judicial Magistrate Ist Class, Banihal attested respective undertakings of the respondents 1 to 4 bearing date 08.04.2023.
22.

The Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban came to put up an office note dated 10.05.2023 and 15.05.2023 detailing therein the fact of judgement and decree dated 30.11.2019 by the Sub Judge, Ramban with respect to acquisitioned land, a pending application for setting aside said judgment and decree in which no stay is in place, pendency of an appeal against the judgement and decree before the Principal District Judge, Ramban in which also no stay is operating and lastly about filing of contempt proceedings by the respondents 1 to 4 before the Court of Sub Judge,
Ramban.

In this note, it also stood mentioned that the respondents 1 to 4 have filed respective undertakings attested by the Judicial Magistrate to the effect that in case the defendants in the case would succeed in the litigation, the respondents 1 to 4 would return the amount released and will abide by the court directions as may be passed.

4 23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In response to this note, the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban lend an approval dated 16.05.2023 which resulted and enabled the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to release the compensation amount purportedly share-wise to the respondents 1 to 4 by transfer of money to their respective bank accounts.
As per the apportionment statement, the respondents 1 to 4 are held entitled to  1,90,27,257/- as sum total of four shares of the compensation.

24. Since the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban's approval is the basis of the release of the compensation amount in favour of the respondents 1 to 4 by reference to their declared status in terms of the civil court decree dated 30.11.2019, as such this court finds that the very proceedings filed by the respondents 1 to 4 for initiation of contempt proceedings against Sh. Harbans Lal,
Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban with power of Collector Land Acquisition, Ramban gets rendered self infructuous admitting of no further proceedings.

Since the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had simply put Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban on a notice to appear in the application of the respondents 1 to 4, it may not lie at any body's end to say that the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had infact directed the disbursement of the compensation to the respondents 1 to 4 or that the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had held Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban to be prima facie guilty of contempt of court decree.

Thus, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban and the Deputy Commissioner Ramban are supposed to have acted on their own understanding and at their own discretion and decision to abide by the decree dated 30/11/2019 of the Sub Judge Ramban and to disburse the compensation share-wise to the respondents 1 to 4.
25.

That being so, even this court is left with no live legal proceedings before the court below to be examined under article 227 of the Constitution of India through this petition which also becomes infructuous only to be disposed of without any adjudication in any manner with respect to merits and demerits of the case on both sides and legality or illegality of the course of action at the end of the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban and the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban which paved way for release of the compensation amount to the extent of their purported share as per the civil court decree.
Thus, this petition is held rendered infructuous.
Sub Judge, Ramban is thus directed to close the proceedings on its File no. 31/Civil/Misc. instituted on 20.03.2023 as being rendered infructuous.

26. However, it is made very clear and is directed that the payment of the compensation amount of 1,90,27,257/- in favour of the respondents 1 to 4 shall ever remain subject to any order as may be passed in the proceeding for setting aside the judgement and decree dated 30.11.2019 pending before the court of Sub Judge, Ramban and/or any further legal proceedings in an appeal/revision as may arise out of final result of said proceeding before the court of Sub Judge, Ramban, or subject to any order/judgement in the pending appeals against the judgement and decree dated 30.11.2019 before the court of Principal District Judge, Ramban.
27.

Further the respondents 1 to 4 are directed to furnish their respective personal bonds before the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to the extent that in case of any order/direction by the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban with respect to repayment of the compensation amount as received by them individually to the extent of their share in purported compliance to the judgement and decree dated Bashir Ahmed Mir vs Gh. Hassan Mir And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172923037/
5 30.11.2019 of the court of Sub Judge, Ramban, the respondents 1 to 4 shall then be bound to repay/return the share-wise amount in favour of the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban without default.
28.

sentences.text: Interim direction/s as passed in this case shall stand vacated.

29. Bank Accounts of the respondents 1 to 4 if freezed by the Bank/s concerned at the direction of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to be restored and the compensation amount, if any,
held back to be restored to the bank accounts of the respondents 1 to 4.
Disposed of accordingly.
